cards.explanation: The answer is that Sarai asks Abram to go to her maidservant Hagar. Sarai, Abram's wife, says, “Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.” Hagar is her Egyptian maidservant. And the verse ends with Abram listening to the voice of Sarai.

The answer is ten, friends. The text says this happens “…after he had lived in Canaan for ten years…” Canaan is the land where Abram and Sarai are living. Then Sarai takes her maidservant Hagar and gives her to Abram to be his wife.

The answer is that Hagar begins to despise Sarai. The text says Hagar “…began to despise her mistress.” Her mistress is Sarai, the woman who owns her household service. Sarai later says Hagar has treated her with contempt (Genesis 16:5).
The answer is True. Sarai says, “May the LORD judge between you and me.” She says it to Abram, her husband. She also says she delivered her servant into his arms.

The answer is that Abram says Hagar is in Sarai's hands. He tells Sarai, “your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai treats Hagar so harshly that Hagar flees. Heavy moment, friends, and I think it's a hard one to read.
The answer is that Hagar flees from Sarai. Sarai treats Hagar so harshly “…that she fled from her.” Hagar, the maidservant, takes off. By the next verse she's out in the desert.

The answer is that the angel tells Hagar to go back and submit to Sarai. The angel of the LORD tells her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.” Hagar has just said she's running away from Sarai, so this is a big ask. The text doesn't say how she feels about it, so I'll only guess: I think that was a lot to hear.

The answer is True. The angel says, “I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.” That's a big promise for a woman who has just been found by a spring in the desert. And it comes from the angel of the LORD himself.

The answer is that the LORD has heard her cry. The angel says to name him Ishmael, “…for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.” The reason is that the LORD heard her. That's the whole reason the angel gives.

The answer is False, friends. The angel says Ishmael will be “…a wild donkey of a man…” and that “he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.” That's the opposite of living in peace. I think this is a heavy part of the passage, and the text doesn't soften it.

The answer is that Hagar calls Him the God who sees her. Hagar says, “You are the God who sees me…” and she gives that name to the LORD who spoke to her. She's a servant who ran into the desert, and she says He sees her. I know a little about feeling unseen, and I think that name hits hard.

The answer is Abram, friends. The text says, “…Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.” Hagar is the mother, but Abram does the naming. Notice that it's the very name the angel gave in verse 11.

The answer is eighty-six. Genesis 16:16 says, “Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.” I can't even remember what I did last year, and the text hands us an exact age. Friends, that's how carefully this story is told.
